title: helper: never block on reading psymail-mini's container
description: Reading ~/Library/Containers/com.psymail.mini/... triggers macOS's 'access data from other apps' consent and the stat blocks until answered — accounts.list hangs forever with no output. Seen 2026-11-18 from both the opencode sandbox and a plain terminal.
design: Do the psymail import once, off the request path, with a deadline (e.g. 3s): if it times out, answer from Moki's own token file and report the import as pending/permission_needed (add an accounts.list field or a helper.status notification) instead of hanging. Prefer reading the exact container path com.psymail.mini rather than globbing ~/Library/Containers/* (globbing stats every app's container). Also add a URLSession timeout (15s) for token refresh/userinfo. Never retry the container read in a tight loop.
acceptance_criteria: accounts.list always answers within ~5s; with container access denied/unanswered it returns Moki-file accounts (or []) plus a permission_needed signal; tests cover the timeout path with an injected slow reader.
notes: post-close: live check showed the deadline never fired (task group waits for all children); fixed by hand
close_reason: landed; live accounts.list still needs the macOS other-app-data consent (container read now bounded and reported as psymailImport)

title: messages lens: read-only email thread pane
description: Selecting a thread in the email list opens it in the right pane read-only: subject header, then each message as an email card (sender, date, body) newest at the bottom, per the design's email card style.
design: renderer/src/lenses/messages/thread/: ThreadPane.tsx (useQuery mail.getThread), EmailCard.tsx. Body rendering: sanitize HTML with DOMPurify (no scripts, no forms, remote images allowed but loaded with referrerpolicy no-referrer), render inside a shadow root (EmailBody.tsx) so email CSS can't leak into the app; dark-mode friendly default text color, links open externally via shell.openExternal through a preload 'openExternal' (http/https only). Plain text bodies rendered as pre-wrap text with links autolinked. Empty state when nothing selected. No reply/archive/mark-read (later beads). Tests: sanitizer strips script/onerror, plain-text rendering.
acceptance_criteria: Clicking a fixture row shows its messages with sanitized HTML rendered and isolated styles; links open in the default browser; nothing selected shows the empty state; typecheck/test/build pass.
notes: round: 2 rounds, accepted
close_reason: landed after one review revision; verified on fixtures via self-capture; real Gmail awaits the macOS other-app-data consent

title: helper: gmail client for label thread lists and thread detail
description: Thin Gmail REST client in the helper: list threads for a label merged across accounts, and fetch one thread's messages. Label scheme mirrors psymail-mini (inbox = INBOX; bundles psymail/<name>).
design: MokiHelperCore/Mail/: GmailClient (URLSession; users.labels.list to resolve label names -> ids per account, cached; users.threads.list?labelIds=..&maxResults=30&pageToken; users.threads.get?format=metadata for list rows (From, Subject, Date headers + snippet + labelIds) fetched with bounded concurrency 8; users.threads.get?format=full for detail). MailService.listThreads(label:String, cursor:[address:pageToken]?) -> {threads:[ThreadSummary], next: cursor?, unreachable:[address], authExpired:[address]} merged newest-first across accounts (pattern from psymail-mini MailSource.MailPage). ThreadSummary {id, account, from:{name,address}, subject, snippet, date ISO8601, unread, messageCount, labelIds}. ThreadDetail {id, account, subject, messages:[{id, from, to, cc, date, html, text, isFromMe}]} with body chosen html>plain, base64url decoded, charset handled. RPC: 'mail.listThreads' {label:'INBOX', cursor?}, 'mail.getThread' {account, id}. Fixture mode env MOKI_FIXTURES=1 serves canned threads (12 rows across 2 accounts incl. one HTML email) with no network so UI work and screenshots don't need sign-in. Mirror the shapes as TS types in packages/protocol (method map). Tests: header parsing, base64url/charset decode, merge ordering, fixture mode.
acceptance_criteria: MOKI_FIXTURES=1 mail.listThreads returns fixture rows; against real accounts it returns the INBOX newest-first with names, subjects, snippets; mail.getThread returns decoded HTML for an HTML email; protocol types match; swift test + pnpm typecheck pass.
notes: round: 2 rounds (+1 relaunch after reading ../psymail-mini aborted the run), accepted
close_reason: landed after one review revision

title: helper: google accounts reusing psymail-mini oauth and tokens
description: The helper can list signed-in Google accounts and mint access tokens, reusing psymail-mini's Desktop OAuth client and its stored refresh tokens so no new sign-in is needed.
design: MokiHelperCore/Google/: OAuthClientConfig loads GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID / GOOGLE_CLIENT_SECRET from (1) env MOKI_GOOGLE_CLIENT_ID/SECRET, (2) ~/dev/psymail-mini/Config/Secrets.xcconfig parsed as 'KEY = value' lines (path overridable by MOKI_PSYMAIL_SECRETS). TokenSource: reads refresh tokens JSON {address: token} from Moki's own file ~/Library/Application Support/Moki/google-tokens.json (0600) and imports from psymail-mini's file: search ~/Library/Containers/*/Data/Library/Application Support/PsymailMini/tokens.json and ~/Library/Application Support/PsymailMini/tokens.json; copies found tokens into Moki's file once (never writes psymail's). AccessTokenCache actor: refresh via POST https://oauth2.googleapis.com/token, cache until expiry-60s; invalid_grant => AppError code 'auth_expired'. Profile via https://www.googleapis.com/oauth2/v2/userinfo (name, picture). RPC: 'accounts.list' -> [{address, name?, photoURL?, status: 'ok'|'auth_expired'}]. Never log or return tokens. Sign-in for new accounts is out of scope (later bead). Tests: xcconfig parsing, token file import/merge, refresh request building with a stubbed URLProtocol.
acceptance_criteria: With psymail-mini signed in, 'accounts.list' over stdio returns the user's Gmail accounts with status ok; with no tokens it returns []; tokens never appear in stdout/stderr; swift test passes.
notes: round: 2 rounds (build + review revision), accepted
close_reason: landed; live accounts.list still needs the macOS other-app-data consent (container read now bounded and reported as psymailImport)

title: helper bridge: spawn helper from main, typed rpc to renderer
description: Electron main spawns the Swift helper, speaks JSON-RPC to it, and exposes a typed, minimal API to the renderer through the preload.
design: packages/protocol: RPC method map type { 'helper.ping': {params: void; result: {ok:boolean; version:string}} , ...} plus notification map; shared error shape {code, message}. apps/desktop/src/main/helper/: HelperProcess (spawn helper binary: dev = helper/.build/debug/moki-helper, built via 'swift build' in a predev script; prod path later), line-buffered stdout parser, pending-request map with per-call timeout (15s), restart with backoff on exit, stderr piped to main log. ipcMain.handle('rpc', (method, params)) forwards; notifications forwarded to renderer via webContents.send('rpc:notify'). Preload: contextBridge.exposeInMainWorld('moki', { call<M>(method, params), on(event, cb) }) typed from protocol. Renderer hook useRpcQuery built on @tanstack/react-query. Unit tests for the line parser and request/response matching with a fake child process. Show helper status (ok / down) in the inspector footer in dev.
acceptance_criteria: pnpm dev builds the helper and launches the app; renderer calls helper.ping and shows version; killing the helper process recovers within a few seconds; tests cover parser + matching.
notes:
from round-1 taste review: preload currently exposes a bespoke ping — replace with window.moki.call/on typed from protocol; declare helper.ping in packages/protocol and drop the MokiProtocolHello placeholder
round: 2 rounds (build + review revision), accepted
close_reason: landed after one review revision

title: scaffold swift helper with stdio json-rpc
description: A SwiftPM executable 'moki-helper' in helper/ that the Electron main process will spawn. Speaks newline-delimited JSON-RPC 2.0 over stdin/stdout; logs only to stderr.
design: helper/Package.swift (swift-tools 6.0, macOS 15+, targets: MokiHelperCore library, moki-helper executable, MokiHelperCoreTests). Core: RPCServer reading lines from stdin, decoding {jsonrpc,id,method,params}, dispatching to a registry [String: Handler] where Handler is (JSONValue params) async throws -> Encodable; writes one JSON line per response; errors map to JSON-RPC error objects (-32601 method not found, -32602 invalid params, -32000 app error with data.code string like 'auth_expired'). Writes must be serialized (actor). Supports server->client notifications {method, params} without id via a Notifier. Built-in methods: 'helper.ping' -> {ok:true, version}. Handlers registered from main.swift so later features add a file + one registration line. Tests: dispatch of ping, unknown method error, malformed JSON error, using an in-memory line transport.
acceptance_criteria: cd helper && swift build && swift test pass; echo '{"jsonrpc":"2.0","id":1,"method":"helper.ping"}' | swift run moki-helper prints a single JSON line with result.ok true; nothing but JSON-RPC lines goes to stdout.
notes:
review: RPCServer.run awaits each request before reading the next line — slow handlers serialize everything; dispatch each line in its own Task
round: 1 round (+1 relaunch after opencode external_directory refusal), accepted with 2 small orchestrator fixes
close_reason: helper scaffold landed; review added concurrent dispatch + silent unknown-method notifications

title: Zen cookie import into the shared web session
description: One-shot import of Zen profile cookies into the shared web session so Docs previews (and future tabs) start signed in. Main-process-only flow; renderer sees status, never values.

Cookie values are secrets: never cross into renderer, logs, or stdout. UI is a single import affordance plus ok/failed per host group; double sign-in inside the guest remains the fallback.

title: Central web-session module: one shared browser session for Docs, Peeks, future tabs
description: Promote the Day tile's webview setup into a central main-process web-session module and a single shared hardened guest component, so Docs previews and future browser tabs share one cookie jar and one set of guards.
design: Single persisted partition for all web content (existing persist:moki-websites), created once in main. Adopt Gooey's hardening: permission handlers deny-all except async clipboard-write, downloads cancel with a notice, http(s) allowlist guards attach plus every main-frame navigation and redirect, popups keep opener in same session and route via deny-to-Peek. Renderer: one hardened guest wrapper (partition, sandbox, contextIsolation, no preload, allowpopups, nav listeners) used by the Docs pane today and tabs tomorrow. Single-instance invariant (Notion IndexedDB trap). Permission broker (camera/mic/notifications/location) and real download routing are explicitly later beads, not this one.
acceptance_criteria: Docs preview and Peek share one session; sign-in in one is visible in the other; non-http(s) guests and popups never load; permissions denied by default with tests; downloads cancel with a notice; scoped main tests green.
notes: round: 4 implementers + 1 unification + 3 revision workers, accepted with review fixes; capture /tmp/mok-docs-lens.png
close_reason: Central web-session module live with attach hardening, single-instance quit, unified allowlist; review fixes applied, gate green.

Reuse the Messages inbox layout classes, not the Figma docs screen. Capture overrides for fixtures.

title: Docs lens plumbing: list recents, preview in shared browser session
description: Docs tab shows three stacked sections (Drive, Notion, Craft), 12 most recent files each. Clicking a file opens it in a full-height pane on the right, mirroring the Messages 2-up. Listing via API, viewing via embedded webview in a shared browser session. Figma docs screen design is ignored.
design: Decisions from planning: single shared persisted web session for Docs previews, Peeks, and future tabs (existing persist:moki-websites), not per-source partitions. One list method with a source param called 3x in parallel, one shared DocItem shape (id, title, source, updatedAt, openUrl). Listing: Drive via helper on existing Google stack, Notion via helper proxy with Keychain token, Craft listing is a spike. Viewing: hardened guest component reused by future tabs, http(s) allowlist enforced twice, deny-to-Peek for popups, deny-all permissions and canceled downloads for v1 with a per-origin permission broker later. Zen cookie import is main-process-only into the shared jar. Single selection across sections replaces the pane per click.

title: helper: list and thread through PsymailEngine
description: Moki helper runs its own Gmail thread listing (threads.list) while psymail lists messages and groups them, so Moki inbox shows threads psymail already routed away. Route Moki mail through psymail PsymailEngine instead of copying the logic.
design: Add PsymailKit as a local SwiftPM dependency of helper (path ../psymail-mini) and raise helper platforms to macOS 26 to match PsymailKit. Define a small MailEngine seam in Moki (page/thread/labelMap) that PsymailEngine conforms to via a Moki-side extension, so tests inject a fake and workers stay offline. Rewrite MailService.listThreads(label,cursor) to: listAccounts for statuses, map label to engine tab (INBOX case-insensitive -> inbox, psymail/<name> -> <name> remainder, unknown bundle -> empty page preserving current InvalidParams swallow), fetch per-account labelMaps through the engine, call engine.page once across all ok accounts, map PsymailRow to ThreadSummary (id=threadId, account=accountAddress, from={fromName,fromAddress}, unread=isUnread, messageCount=threadCount, date=ISO8601, keep snippet/subject/labelIds). Keep getThread on the existing Gmail detail fetch (no psymail change, no subject/to-cc loss); delete only the list path (listThreadIDs/threadSummary/fetchSummaries/summarize + resolveLabelID cache) and keep fetchDetail+parsing. Keep GoogleAccountsService/token store as the access-token source (engine token closure calls accounts.accessToken). Keep RPC shapes unchanged so the renderer is untouched. Single shared engine per MailService (emitted tracking is per-tab; note psy-knn0 interleaved-listing limit as known).
acceptance_criteria: swift build --package-path helper passes on macOS 26 with PsymailKit linked; swift test --package-path helper passes with list tests running against a fake engine (no network); unknown bundle label yields empty threads (not an error); auth_unconfigured still throws; unreachable/authExpired per-account mapping preserved; MOKI_FIXTURES path untouched; pnpm typecheck/test/build unaffected (no protocol change).
notes: round: 1 implementer (initial) + 1 revision worker (review fixes 2+3) + 2 reviewers (taste, correctness); no worker hit its cap (30k initial / 15k revision); 3 full gates, all green except pre-existing opencode-contract-link env failure (filed mok-05p)
close_reason: Helper lists through PsymailEngine (generic INBOX/psymail label mapping, token store kept, RPC unchanged, detail stays on Gmail full fetch). Review fixes in: RFC2047 subject/name decode + (No subject) fallback, empty-cursor normalization. Known gap: labelMap 401/403 classifies as unreachable until psy-isrj ships a typed psymail error; mirror seam structs kept as the offline-test boundary.

title: harness add: inject resolved root into opencode.json external_directory
description: Local opencode.json now allows the resolved harness root for worker reads (mok-y3q), but harness add copies template/stubs/opencode.json verbatim, so future checkouts won't inherit it. Change install.sh to append the resolved-root allow entry when writing opencode.json. Lives in the harness-starter repo.
design: In harness-starter commands/add.sh, after the reference copy loop, inject the resolved harness root (harness_reference_root) into a newly-added opencode.json permission.external_directory via python3 JSON edit; if opencode.json was skipped as pre-existing, print a nudge with the exact entry instead of touching it. Extend harness_normalise in commands/lib/install.sh to strip external_directory entries that point at a live harness checkout (dir containing template/.harness-root), so drift-compare ignores the host-specific entry where valid and flags it where stale.
acceptance_criteria: Fresh harness add into a scratch target writes opencode.json with the resolved-root allow entry; re-run over an existing file prints the nudge without modifying; normalise strips the entry iff it resolves to a live checkout; bash -n clean on both scripts.
notes: round: direct implementation by orchestrator (hand-sized; no workers spawned). gate + taste/correctness review before commit.
close_reason: superseded by starter bead har-ttnm, whose runtime-grant design (agent.py per-role allow + deny, with tests) is strictly better than add-time injection into committed config. Prototyped injection + drift-normalise, proved e2e, then reverted in favor of har-ttnm. Moki keeps its local opencode.json allow as the interim workaround.

title: ThreadList auto-select test flakes in full-suite runs
description: ThreadList.test.tsx 'auto-selects the first row' fails intermittently in full pnpm test runs (selected-lit not yet applied at assertion) while passing in isolation 3/3 and in other full runs. Same suite family as the midnight-boundary formatRelativeTime flake. Likely selection-effect timing or cross-test query-cache bleed. Make it deterministic (await the selected state instead of asserting synchronously, or isolate the query cache per test).
design: Make ThreadList auto-select deterministic without changing product behavior unless needed. In ThreadList.test.tsx await the selected-lit state (waitFor/findBy) instead of asserting synchronously after findByText; ensure query cache isolation per test (RpcProvider already makes a fresh QueryClient per mount via useState — verify no cross-test bleed). Touch useSelectedThread only if the race needs it (e.g. initialise selection during render).
acceptance_criteria: ThreadList.test.tsx 'auto-selects the first row' passes consistently across repeated full-suite runs (3x pnpm test green); no other tests broken.
notes: round: 4-worker implementer round + orchestrator revision; reviewers taste+correctness clean on second packet pass. worker caps 15/20/30/25k; revision + gate + reviews on orchestrator.
close_reason: auto-select awaited via waitFor; green across repeated full-suite runs, no product change.

title: explore: make the Moki UI feel alive and dynamic
description:
Exploration for later, not v1.

Idea: make the Moki UI feel alive and dynamic. Many small motions all happening at once; through the mere fact of it all happening together it creates cohesion, even though it's essentially chaos.

- Things askew and shifted in perspective relative to each other; nothing really straight-lined.
- On hover, a very subtle light follows the mouse, and the panel moves in 3D space to lean toward the mouse.
- Clouds drifting by, covering the UI for a second.
- Goo moving through that pushes the menu items, tab bar or sidebar items a little as it passes.
- Sidebar items rotated weirdly and askew.
- A sunrise and sunset vibe, naturally going from light to dark theme through the day.

Full write-up: the Moki page in Notion, section "Make it feel alive".

title: explore: Claude builds custom lenses inside Moki, Notion as the data store
description:
Exploration for later, not v1.

Idea: let Claude build new lenses directly inside Moki. Claude hooks into Moki and uses Moki's own interface (shell, lens registry, ui/ primitives) to spin up quick custom experiences, with Notion as the data store behind them.

Ties into the earlier plan for Claude to quickly spin up custom UIs presenting Notion data, reusing the starter-kit design system from the Fusebox migration work.

Open questions to explore: how Claude hooks in (helper RPC, a lens SDK, generated lens folders); how a generated lens is sandboxed and registered; Notion access through the helper (tokens stay native); how the starter-kit design system maps onto Moki's tokens and primitives.

After something lands (commit): relaunch the app WITHOUT the auto-quit capture flag, re-capture the affected screens, eyeball them, and LEAVE THE APP OPEN at the end of the round so the user finds it running. Kill stale instances first (pigs pile up and hold the helper).

Swift withTaskGroup waits for ALL children before returning, even after cancelAll; awaiting Task.value ignores cancellation — a 'timeout race' built on a task group never times out. Race with a once-only continuation instead.
